items.title: DNS resolution end-to-end
items.overview: Stub resolver → recursive resolver → TLD → authoritative. Caching at each layer affects TTL and propagation delays.
selfCheckQuestions: What record types map hostname to IPv4 vs IPv6?
Why can DNS cause stale failover?
items.youtubeSearch: how DNS works step by step
items.whyGoogle: Every Google service starts with a resolved endpoint—debugging starts here.

items.title: TCP handshake and teardown
items.overview: SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK establish connection. FIN/FIN-ACK close gracefully; RST aborts. Three-way handshake costs one RTT before data.
items.whyGoogle: Connection setup dominates small request latency at scale.

items.title: UDP use cases and limits
items.overview: Connectionless, unordered, unreliable—good for DNS, QUIC base, real-time media when app handles loss.
selfCheckQuestions: Why doesn't video always use TCP?
When would you add reliability on UDP?
items.whyGoogle: Choosing transport correctly signals systems maturity.

items.title: HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2
items.overview: HTTP/2 multiplexes streams on one TCP connection with header compression. HTTP/1.1 needed multiple connections or pipelining (rare).
selfCheckQuestions: Does HTTP/2 eliminate head-of-line blocking entirely?
items.whyGoogle: Frontends and APIs at Google heavily use HTTP/2 and gRPC.

items.title: HTTPS and TLS handshake
items.overview: TLS negotiates cipher suite, authenticates server via certificates, establishes session keys. TLS 1.3 reduces round trips.
selfCheckQuestions: Why terminate TLS at load balancer?
items.whyGoogle: Security questions expect TLS literacy, not cipher memorization.

items.title: Load balancing algorithms
items.overview: Round robin, least connections, consistent hash for stickiness. L4 vs L7 balancers see different headers and paths.
checklist: Discuss active vs passive health checks
items.whyGoogle: Google frontends are LB-heavy; interviews probe failure handling.

items.title: CDN caching and cache keys
items.overview: Edge caches static and cacheable API responses. Cache-Control, ETag, and Vary headers control behavior.
checklist: Explain cache hit vs miss path
items.youtubeSearch: CDN how it works cache control
items.whyGoogle: Serving billions of users requires CDN mental models.

items.title: WebSockets vs long polling
items.overview: WebSockets upgrade to full-duplex channel; long polling simulates push with repeated requests. SSE one-way server push over HTTP.
selfCheckQuestions: How to heartbeat detect dead connections?
items.whyGoogle: Real-time products (chat, docs) need transport trade-off fluency.

items.title: JWT structure and validation
items.overview: Header.payload.signature base64url. Validate alg, exp, aud, iss; never trust payload without signature verify.
selfCheckQuestions: Why not store PII in JWT?
items.whyGoogle: Identity flows intersect many Google cloud and API designs.

items.title: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow
items.overview: User consents; client exchanges code for tokens using client secret or PKCE for public clients.
items.whyGoogle: Google identity products implement these flows at massive scale.

items.title: Timeouts and deadline propagation
items.overview: Every outbound call needs a timeout derived from user-facing SLO. Propagate deadlines via context/metadata across hops.
selfCheckQuestions: Client timeout vs server timeout mismatch symptom?
Why shorter than client at each hop?
items.whyGoogle: Tail latency control is core Google SRE culture.

items.title: Retries, backoff, and jitter
items.overview: Retry idempotent operations with exponential backoff and jitter to avoid thundering herds. Cap retries and fail fast.
selfCheckQuestions: Which HTTP methods safe to retry?
items.whyGoogle: Resilience patterns are expected in design and coding discussions.

items.title: Circuit breakers and bulkheads
items.overview: Stop calling failing dependencies; isolate thread pools to limit blast radius. Half-open probes recovery.
items.whyGoogle: Large distributed systems fail partially—patterns are interview staples.

items.title: NAT and connection tracking
items.overview: NAT maps private IPs to public ports; state tables expire. Affects peer-to-peer and long idle connections.
items.whyGoogle: Debugging connectivity issues requires NAT awareness.

items.title: HTTP status codes and semantics
items.overview: 2xx success, 4xx client fault, 5xx server fault. 429 rate limit, 503 overload with Retry-After.
checklist: Pick codes for common API errors
items.whyGoogle: API design clarity is evaluated in backend interviews.

items.title: CORS and browser security
items.overview: Browsers enforce same-origin; CORS headers permit cross-origin XHR/fetch. Preflight for non-simple requests.
items.whyGoogle: Web-facing Google products require solid browser networking knowledge.

items.title: QUIC and HTTP/3 overview
items.overview: QUIC runs over UDP with integrated TLS 1.3 and stream multiplexing without TCP HOL blocking.
items.whyGoogle: Google pioneered QUIC—shows cultural and technical alignment.

items.title: Reverse proxy vs forward proxy
items.overview: Reverse proxy sits before servers (nginx, Envoy); forward proxy for client egress (corporate). Different routing goals.
items.whyGoogle: Edge architecture questions assume proxy vocabulary.

items.title: gRPC vs REST trade-offs
items.overview: gRPC uses HTTP/2, protobuf, streaming RPCs—great internal; REST+json broader external compatibility.
checklist: Pick REST vs gRPC for public API
items.whyGoogle: Google invented gRPC—common in internal service discussions.

items.title: TCP congestion control (conceptual)
items.overview: Algorithms (Cubic, BBR) adjust send rate based on loss and delay. Affects throughput on lossy or bufferbloated links.
items.whyGoogle: Performance debugging sometimes reaches transport layer.

items.title: Anycast and geo routing
items.overview: Same IP announced from multiple PoPs; BGP routes to nearest. Used by large DNS and CDN providers.
checklist: Mention Google global load balancing idea
items.whyGoogle: Global traffic management is central to Google infrastructure.

items.title: Rate limiting headers and 429
items.overview: Token bucket and leaky bucket algorithms. Communicate limits via Retry-After and rate limit headers.
items.whyGoogle: Protecting shared APIs is a classic design + implementation topic.

items.title: IPv4 exhaustion and IPv6
items.overview: IPv6 larger address space; dual stack common. Format and zone IDs for link-local.
items.whyGoogle: Modern services must plan for IPv6 in infrastructure.

items.title: Cookies, sessions, and SameSite
items.overview: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite mitigate XSS and CSRF. Session IDs server-side vs client JWT trade-offs.
items.whyGoogle: Web security basics protect billions of Google accounts.

items.title: Tracing a request through the stack
items.overview: Browser → DNS → TCP/TLS → LB → app → DB/cache → response. Correlate with trace IDs and structured logs.
checklist: Tie to debugging slow API report
items.whyGoogle: End-to-end thinking distinguishes strong backend candidates.
